metadata.label: scenario estimate, not validated
metadata.purpose: Compare candidate aquaponics unit configurations on revenue per output unit versus labour + electricity cost per output unit, to find which designs could carry heating, fixed costs and consumables. Not a go/no-go.
metadata.geography_basis: Two locations side by side (Ajit, 2026-11-25): Netherlands and India. Each location carries its own price, wage, electricity and saleability inputs in its own currency; physical intensities (yield, labour hours, kWh per m2) are shared.

origin_vocabulary.sourced_candidate: read from an external source in this pass; candidate until Ajit approves it
origin_vocabulary.derived_candidate: arithmetic on cited values only; no new assumption added
origin_vocabulary.transferred_candidate: sourced value applied to a different crop or context than its source; flagged as a transfer
origin_vocabulary.missing: no source yet; left null and reported as a gap

source_tier_vocabulary.tier_1: official and university sources (Trusted Source Map)
source_tier_vocabulary.tier_3: commercial manuals or catalogues, strict gating
source_tier_vocabulary.derived: arithmetic or simulation on the above

state_inputs_caveats: Wages are legal minimum plus a burden proxy, not market wages
Paid hours per day are 8 in every state; sourced only for Telangana (overtime beyond 8 h)
Electricity is energy charge only; fixed/demand charges, duty and fuel surcharges are excluded
Which tariff category an aquaponic unit falls into is unknown in every state, so low = agri/horticulture-type category, high = commercial-type category
No state-specific basil price exists; all four share the all-India band

heidemann_bailey_2015_uvi_economics.citation: Heidemann and Bailey 2015, Commercial Aquaponics Case Study #3: Economic Analysis of the UVI Commercial Aquaponics System (SARE, draft AEC 2015-18), Tables 7, 8, 11
heidemann_bailey_2015_uvi_economics.confidence_reason: Measured operating records from a long-running research system, but a draft report, USD 2014, tropical site, and labour and electricity are whole-system with no crop split.
heidemann_bailey_2015_uvi_economics.cross_check: Grow area 214 m2 matches Rakocy et al. 2004 (canon). Labour share pattern (largest cost) agrees with Tokunaga et al. and Quagrainie et al.

rakocy_2004_uvi_tilapia_basil_acta_hort_.citation: Rakocy et al. 2004, Aquaponic production of tilapia and basil: comparing a batch and staggered cropping system, Acta Hort 648
rakocy_2004_uvi_tilapia_basil_acta_hort_.confidence_reason: Primary trial data, already accepted as canon (CROP_0004) by Ajit on 2026-11-25.
rakocy_2004_uvi_tilapia_basil_acta_hort_.cross_check: Simulator calibrated to the same anchor (PR #1).

tokunaga_2015_hawaii_aquaponics_economic.citation: Tokunaga, Tamaru, Ako and Leung, Economics of Small-scale Commercial Aquaponics in Hawai'i (CTSA report Nov 2013; published 2015, J World Aquaculture Society). Read: ctsa.org/files/publications/HawaiiAquaponicsEconomics_Nov13.pdf, Tables 1, 3, 7, 8, 12
tokunaga_2015_hawaii_aquaponics_economic.confidence_reason: Model farm built from a survey of operating Hawaii farms (fieldwork 2012), with an itemised labour task table. It is a representative model, not one farm's records, and it is lettuce, not basil. The journal version is peer-reviewed; the report version was read.
tokunaga_2015_hawaii_aquaponics_economic.cross_check: Labour share of operating cost (48%) agrees with SRAC 5006 summary (46%) and Quagrainie et al. (62-67%). Labour cost line ($31,842) reproduces from 2,326 h x $9.75 x 1.40.

quagrainie_purdue_indiana_aquaponics.citation: Quagrainie et al., Economic analysis of aquaponics production in Indiana (Purdue Agricultural Economics), Tables 6-9
quagrainie_purdue_indiana_aquaponics.confidence_reason: Hypothetical representative farms, not measured, no grow area given, no price year, and several internal inconsistencies (Table 2 total, investment claim, NPV values in conclusion vs Table 5).
quagrainie_purdue_indiana_aquaponics.cross_check: Labour dominates operating cost, consistent with Tokunaga et al. and UVI. Scale effect direction (unit cost falls with size) agrees with SRAC 5006's general statement that scale economies are weaker than in other aquaculture.

zappernick_2022_techno_economic.citation: Zappernick et al. 2022, Techno-economic analysis of a recirculating tilapia-lettuce aquaponics system, Journal of Cleaner Production 365, 132753, Sec. 2.2.2
zappernick_2022_techno_economic.confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed, but only the methods section was read verbatim; total labour hours and later results came from an extracted summary and are not used here.
zappernick_2022_techno_economic.cross_check: Harvest rate of 30 plants per hour is far slower than the Tokunaga task table implies for lettuce; treated as a small-system bound only.

cbi_2024_fresh_culinary_herbs.citation: CBI (Netherlands Enterprise Agency programme), Entering the European market for fresh culinary herbs, last updated 18 January 2024, Table 1
cbi_2024_fresh_culinary_herbs.confidence_reason: Government-backed market study, but basil wholesale figures are price-list examples from March 2020 (over 5 years old) and the bundle range is for herbs in general.
cbi_2024_fresh_culinary_herbs.cross_check: Same figures as the repo research pack (First-slice basil wholesale economics input pack).

vbt_landbouwcijfers_vlaanderen_weekly_pr.citation: Departement Landbouw en Visserij (Vlaanderen), VBT weekly price information, vegetables, weeks 24/2024, 50/2024, 24/2025 (landbouwcijfers.vlaanderen.be)
vbt_landbouwcijfers_vlaanderen_weekly_pr.confidence_reason: Official realised auction producer prices, but the PDF text extraction was column-scrambled, the per-product unit is not printed (lettuce is probably per head), and the lettuce type behind 'Sla' is not stated. Belgian, not Dutch.
vbt_landbouwcijfers_vlaanderen_weekly_pr.cross_check: Order of magnitude (well under EUR 1 per head) is far below the US farm-gate lettuce prices in Tokunaga et al. (USD 2.15/lb) and Zappernick et al. (USD 2.05/head organic), which is expected for a Low Countries auction channel.

research_pack_nl_inputs.citation: data/sources/research_reports/markdown/First-slice basil wholesale economics input pack.md (CBS electricity 500-2,000 MWh/yr band; Dutch greenhouse CAO 1 July 2025 plus employer burden)
research_pack_nl_inputs.confidence_reason: Underlying sources are official (CBS, CAO), read through a non-canonical research pack; the burden loading on top of the CAO wage is a pack estimate.
research_pack_nl_inputs.cross_check: Same values used by the Farm inputs thread (farm_viability_inputs_v0.json).

basil_crop_cycle_simulation.citation: data/simulation/results/basil_raft_crop_cycle_uvi_feed_ratio_28d.json (UVI feed ratio, 2.00 kg/m2 per harvest after PR #6 and PR #11)
basil_crop_cycle_simulation.confidence_reason: Simulation output calibrated to the UVI anchor; nitrification (PR #6) and nitrate uptake (PR #11) models are candidates pending review.
basil_crop_cycle_simulation.cross_check: Matches the UVI batch per-harvest yield (2.0 kg/m2, canon CROP_0003).

research_pack_india_inputs.citation: data/sources/research_reports/markdown/First-slice basil wholesale economics input pack.md, India section (Andhra Pradesh hydroponic basil study 2025; Chief Labour Commissioner agriculture minimum wages April 2025 plus EPF 12% and ESIC 3.25%; TNERC HT Tariff I 2025; ECB reference rate 20 April 2026)
research_pack_india_inputs.confidence_reason: Wage floor and tariff anchor are official, but the price band is one hydroponic study's sale price (INR 1,000/kg) with operator haircuts for the lower points, the first-wholesale stage is unproven, and the tariff depends on state and category.
research_pack_india_inputs.cross_check: Same values as the repo research pack; the India sale price anchor converts to about EUR 9.1/kg, inside the Dutch band, which is plausible for a premium fresh-herb channel but not confirmed.

india_working_day_hours.citation: Factories Act 1948 s.54 (adult working day at most 9 hours) and the common 8-hour working day under Indian minimum-wage rules
india_working_day_hours.confidence_reason: Used only to convert a per-day wage into a per-hour wage; the real paid hours per day on an Indian farm are not sourced and need Ajit's check.

labour_h_per_m2_yr.derivation: Hawaii model-farm (low) to UVI whole-system (high) intensity. Reported as owner hours needed, not as a cash cost.

heating.context: Dutch greenhouse sector average total energy use was 0.99 GJ/m2 in 2024 (WUR Energiemonitor 2025-150, provisional, all crops incl. lit crops). Not crop-specific, so not applied.

annualised_capex.context: Only USD references found: Tokunaga et al. model farm USD 217,078 total investment for 1,141.6 m2 raceway (about USD 190 per m2, 2012); Zappernick et al. about USD 69,400 for a 62-63 m2 grow bed (about USD 1,110 per m2, 2019); UVI owner-built depreciation USD 3,420/yr for 214 m2 (2014). No EUR or Dutch build cost is sourced.

consumables_feed_seed_fingerlings_water.context: Tokunaga et al. Year 1: feed USD 7,216, water 4,155, seed 1,122, chemicals 1,209 for 1,141.6 m2 (USD, 2012). Not converted.

fish_revenue.context: SRAC 5006 (Engle 2015) summarises that the fish portion of studied systems was often not profitable, so fish revenue is treated as a cost offset to research later, not a design driver.

saleable_harvest_mass_kg_note: Not populated. Per-m2 saleable output here is a scenario estimate inside the calculator, not a value for that field.

wage_per_hour.note: Burdened Dutch greenhouse production labour. Owner hours are a separate decision (see owner-operated configuration).
